Opinion on competitive gaming? Do you fit in the competitive type of mindset? Which genre do you have the most competitive experience in?

Competitive gaming is a lot like the end-game of any other kind of hobby or pursuit, in that it requires a rather substantial investment of time.

Beyond straight up natural talent, the time required to learn all the ins and outs of any given game can be incredibly long depending on the learning curve, skill ceiling etc.

Due to this, it's been relegated almost exclusively to younger people or those who have an abundance of it's most necessary resource, time.

There are some sub genres however, where older players are more competitive, a good example of which is classic arcade gaming where many of the world record holders are much older as a whole than say the average CS:GO player.

How competitive gaming evolves from here and whether or not it becomes successful will largely rest on it's acceptance by the main stream as a viable career choice / choice for entertainment and if/when more people are able to dedicate more time to it.

As for my personal experience, I've competed against some of the best in the world on some titles and I was at one point during the 1.6 era of CS a member of a team in the CAL-M tier. I enjoyed the atmosphere and competition of those days and it was exciting to hit the top tier of a skill plateau in a game where you get to see how much tactics play into things. That said, the sheer time investment to learn said tactics and build rapport with your team conflicted so heavily with real obligations that it was prohibitive.

These days, the barrier to entry is much lower, considering how some even manage to earn a living playing games solely by streaming, so it seems pretty likely that as a niche it will continue to grow, whether or not it can expand beyond that remains to be seen.
Competitive gaming is fun to watch. I enjoy the streams from Blizzcon (SC BW before, SC2 now, a little WoW) every year. Better show than sports.

Honestly, I find it kinda stupid. I prefer real, physical competition that doesn't rely on ping counts/actions per minute/whatever else. Competitive gaming just seems so pathetic to me. These people literally train for a computer game...I enjoy a nice round of multiplayer as much as the next guy but professional Dota? LoL? Gimmie a break.
I really enjoy it, I am a low rank in CSGO and while I dont have the typical mindset as in I dont care about winning or losing I do enjoy the more serious side to it.
